_comment.1: WFS matched-filter variant of steering_par_fsp.json for the 32x32 ASI290MM ROI.
_comment.2: The 3x3 grid has 6x6 px cells and a 2 px search margin: a 22x22 tracked window, leaving 5 px guard on each side of the ROI when centred.
_comment.3: Rolling shutter is handled by anyloop:fit_com's motion model, not by detect-and-reject. A shear threshold is necessarily a velocity threshold, so it drops frames at the fast part of every oscillation and keeps the turning points -- phase-correlated dropout that leaves the loop open exactly when the beam is moving fastest and biases fsp's identified model. Fitting the slope removes that failure mode rather than tuning it.
_comment.4: Catastrophic frames are contained, not guessed: a fit whose amplitude collapses or whose sigma hits a bound is rejected, the last output is held, and FSP holds its previous command without learning from the held coordinate. Frames are NOT rejected for shear.
_comment.5: FSP K/delay are inherited from the 2026-07-31 CoM parport Bodes: the image-normalized scale is unchanged, so small-signal gain and phase carry over. The DC setpoint DOES now match center_of_mass, unlike the wfs_com variant: fit_com reports absolute position, so init_y/init_x only seed the search and no pointing offset is absorbed. Treat K/delay as bring-up values: re-run full-band Bodes with this sensor before unattended closure.
_comment.6: Safety: verify both feedback signs with a push test. Normal FSP authority is +/-1 V; +/-10 V is available only to transient recovery and is matched by the downstream backstop.

pipeline._choice: fit_com CHOSEN 2026-08-06 on measured data, re-confirmed on the stable centred beam. Same 60 s capture: fit_com hf 0.271 px / 11.4% rejected, wfs_com hf 0.814 / 79.9%, thresholded center_of_mass hf 0.639 / 22.9%. hf is the frame-to-frame difference, i.e. what the loop must reject -- fit_com is 3x quieter than wfs_com. wfs_com's rejection is NOT a geometry error: re-run at 3x3 and 5x5 grids with 6/8/14 px cells it stayed 82-88%, and only reached 35.9% with every quality gate disabled. Cost p50 17.4 us / p99 27.0 us against a 433 us frame period. The 11.4% rejection is the 4.7 Hz source modulation, not the tracker -- see com_survey.json.
pipeline._provenance: MEASURED 2026-08-06 by contrib/com_survey_run.sh over a 60 s / 138600-frame capture at 64x64, exp 400, gain 0, fs 2310 Hz, with the ROI auto-centred first (find_roi put it at 1088/406, beam landing at (28.39, 29.95) against a 31.5 centre -- the residual is the 4-px/2-px ASI ROI grid, not an error): beam sigma 6.55 px / FWHM 15.43, amplitude 213.9 over background 1.74, saturation 2.68%. window 55 = +/-4 sigma; sigma_min/max and min_amplitude are 0.3x/4x/0.1x of measured, which is how com_survey derives its own suggestions. RE-RUN contrib/com_survey_run.sh AND RE-DERIVE after any refocus or source change -- these are beam properties. An EARLIER set (sigma 6.31, window 53) was taken while the beam was being moved by hand and is superseded.
pipeline._shutter: NOTE ON THE CHOPPED SOURCE: the center_of_mass this replaces used ref_cut to drop frames the rolling shutter cuts through the source's on-window. fit_com has no ref_cut. It handles those frames through robust (Tukey) reweighting and the min_amplitude gate instead, and the 20.8% rejection above ALREADY INCLUDES them -- that number was measured on these same chopped frames. Watch it if the chop duty changes.

params._budget: max_us 25 is ABOVE the measured p99 of 27.2 us only just -- expect the guard to bite on the slowest few percent of frames, truncating those fits to fewer LM iterations. The survey's numbers were taken at the 10 us DEFAULT, so 25 lets the fit converge FURTHER than what was benchmarked, not less. Set 0 to remove the cap entirely, at the cost of a variable measurement latency that a fixed-delay model downstream will read as a wobbling loop delay.
params._reacquire: reacquire_after 300 frames = 130 ms at 2310 Hz, NOT the 10 that com_survey's benchmark harness uses. This is the difference between the two failure paths downstream. A rejected frame (fsp.c:2141) holds the actuator command and advances the delay and modal state without training the observer -- correct for a frame the beam was briefly too dim to fit. BEAM_LOST (fsp.c:1960) zeroes the output, calls fsp_reset_after_beam_loss (xhat, the ucmd delay ring, plant and drift states, all transient state) and ramps back over beam_recover_ramp 0.5 s. MEASURED 2026-08-06: the 4.70 Hz source modulation produces 6 dark stretches per second, median 3 frames but p90 49 and max 201 (87 ms). At reacquire_after 10 every stretch over 4.3 ms takes the catastrophic path -- about 9 full observer resets per second, each starting a 0.5 s recovery that the next reset interrupts, so the loop never converges and the log fills with 'fit failed'. 300 sits above the longest observed stretch, so modulation routes to the hold path and BEAM_LOST means the beam is actually gone. Cost: a genuine loss takes 130 ms to declare instead of 4.3 ms. RE-DERIVE THIS from the dark-stretch distribution if the source changes; on a CW source it can go back down.

pipeline._delay_warning: Inherited CoM bring-up estimate: x 2.763 frames, y 2.624 frames at fs~3788. A WFS-specific 5-300 Hz Bode is required before treating these values as measured; never estimate delay from a 10-30 Hz small-signal sweep.
pipeline._K_warning: Inherited small-signal gains at the same ROI and normalized coordinate convention: Kx=4.05, Ky=3.646. Re-measure if the WFS/CoM response ratio is not unity in a push test or Bode plateau.

params._transient_off_2026_08_07: TRANSIENT PATH DISABLED 2026-08-07 (was 6.0). transient_sigma is the master switch -- it defaults to 0 and every other transient validation in fsp.c:1370-1390 is gated on transient_sigma > 0, so the whole detection/recovery path goes inert while all the tuning below is preserved verbatim for re-enabling. Off for now because the plant it would act against is not currently characterised: K and the delay predate today's refocus, and the scale sign is inferred from sweep phase rather than a push test. A modal event controller that fires with authority transient_clamp 10.0 against a mis-signed or mis-scaled plant is the worst possible time to find that out. Restore 6.0 once a push test and fresh sweeps are in. NOTE: transient_shadow_mu MUST BE ZEROED TOO. Its validation (fsp.c:1356) is gated on transient_shadow_mu > 0, NOT on transient_sigma, so leaving shadow_mu at 0.01 with transient_sigma 0 is a half-disabled state that fails init outright: 'transient shadow recovery requires transient_sigma > 0'. Both go to 0 together; restore 6.0 / 0.01 together.

pipeline._comment: Same zero-bias parport mapping used to measure the inherited plant model: y positive on DACA, x negative on DACB.

params._scale_sign_2026_08_07: SIGN CORRECTED 2026-08-07 to [-1, 1] = [ch0 y, ch1 x], matching steering_par_fsp.json and attenuation_par_fsp.json. Both bode sweeps measure a POSITIVE, in-phase K with x at +1.0 and y at -1.0 (phase at 5 Hz +0.037 rad x / +0.028 rad y, i.e. ~0 not ~pi), which is the sign convention fsp's u = -phi_hat/K assumes. The previous signs would have been positive feedback on both axes. CONFIRMED CORRECT ON THE BENCH 2026-08-07. Fix any future change here rather than by flipping K.
